title: Supervisor Flags & Restart Strategies: one_for_one, rest_for_one, and one_for_all
solutionExplanation: Validates supervisor flag arguments, maps architectural topology descriptors to OTP restart strategy atoms, and calculates fractional restart frequency budgets.

typesSpec: SupFlags = #{strategy => strategy(), intensity => non_neg_integer(), period => pos_integer()}
otpDocCards.description: Initializes the supervisor, defining the restart strategy, crash frequency limit, and initial child specifications.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) initialization. Executed synchronously during supervisor:start_link.

mentalModelCheck.question: In a supervision tree with children [db_pool, pricing_cache, order_gateway] under rest_for_one, what happens when pricing_cache crashes?

options.label: pricing_cache and downstream order_gateway are restarted; upstream db_pool is untouched.
options.explanation: rest_for_one terminates and restarts the crashed worker and any worker started after it in the child spec list, preserving upstream dependencies.

options.label: All three workers (db_pool, pricing_cache, order_gateway) are terminated and restarted.
options.explanation: That is the behavior of one_for_all, not rest_for_one.

options.label: Only pricing_cache is restarted; order_gateway continues running uninterrupted.
options.explanation: That is the behavior of one_for_one, which would leave order_gateway holding dead cache references.

options.label: db_pool and pricing_cache restart; order_gateway is untouched.
options.explanation: rest_for_one restarts downstream workers, never preceding upstream workers.
